title: Maize nitrogen deficiency symptoms
text: Nitrogen deficiency in maize shows as uniform yellowing starting from older lower leaves while the midrib often stays greener. Stunted plants and pale leaves reduce yield if not corrected. Split nitrogen application at planting and knee-high stage improves uptake in leaching-prone soils.

title: Common bean rust management
text: Bean rust appears as small reddish-brown pustules on leaf undersides in cool humid weather. Remove heavily infected debris, avoid overhead irrigation at dusk, and use certified clean seed. Fungicide sprays may be justified when rust exceeds five percent leaf area in commercial plots.

title: Cassava mosaic disease
text: Cassava mosaic causes leaf distortion, chlorotic mosaic patterns, and stunted stems spread by whiteflies. Plant virus-free cuttings from certified nurseries and rogue out infected plants early. Intercrop with non-hosts and avoid consecutive cassava on the same field without resistant varieties.

title: Fall armyworm in maize
text: Fall armyworm larvae feed in the whorl leaving ragged window-pane damage and frass pellets. Scout twice weekly at early vegetative stage and treat when more than ten percent of plants are infested. Rotate insecticide modes of action and conserve natural enemies along field margins.

title: Stem borer in sorghum
text: Stem borers tunnel inside sorghum stalks causing deadheart in seedlings and broken stems at maturity. Destroy crop residues after harvest, plant early with the rains, and consider push-pull trap crops. Parasitoid wasps increase when flowering strips border the field.

title: Aphids on vegetable seedlings
text: Aphids cluster on tender shoots causing leaf curl and honeydew that leads to sooty mould. Monitor nursery beds daily, use reflective mulch, and wash colonies off with soapy water at low pressure. Avoid broad-spectrum sprays that kill ladybird beetles and lacewings.

title: Soil acidity and liming
text: Acidic ferralsols bind phosphorus and limit legume nodulation below pH 5.5. Apply agricultural lime based on soil test, incorporating before planting season. Combine liming with organic matter to improve buffer capacity and moisture retention.

title: Cover crops for soil structure
text: Cover crops like mucuna or lablab reduce erosion and suppress weeds between main seasons. Terminate covers before they set hard seed and leave residues as surface mulch. Leguminous covers add nitrogen when biomass is incorporated or left as mulch.

title: Compost quality for smallholders
text: Well-made compost should be dark, crumbly, and free of undecomposed stalks or foul odour. Layer green and brown materials, keep piles moist, and turn every two weeks. Apply compost in planting basins to improve water infiltration on crusted soils.

title: Climate-smart planting dates
text: Align planting with the onset of reliable rains using local rainfall calendars or forecasts. Short-season drought-tolerant maize varieties reduce risk when the rainy season shortens. Stagger planting across plots to spread exposure to mid-season dry spells.

title: Heat stress in livestock
text: Heat stress lowers milk yield and fertility; provide shade, night grazing, and clean water ad libitum. Select breeds adapted to local temperature extremes and avoid working animals in peak afternoon heat. Sprinkle water in holding pens only where ventilation prevents humidity buildup.

title: Index-based insurance basics
text: Weather-index insurance pays when rainfall or vegetation indices cross predefined thresholds. Understand basis risk: payouts may not match individual field losses. Combine insurance with water harvesting and diversified crops to reduce livelihood shocks.

title: Rainwater harvesting from roofs
text: Roof catchment systems channel rain into screened tanks for supplemental irrigation. First-flush diverters reduce dust and bird droppings entering storage. Size tanks to expected dry-season irrigation demand and maintain mosquito-proof covers.

title: Drip irrigation for vegetables
text: Drip lines deliver water at the root zone, cutting losses from evaporation and runoff. Filter water to prevent emitter clogging and flush lines weekly in sandy soils. Mulch beds to keep soil moisture stable between irrigation cycles.

title: Contour bunds on slopes
text: Contour bunds slow runoff and increase infiltration on sloping fields. Stabilise bunds with grass strips and repair breaches after heavy storms. Plant deep-rooted perennials on upper contours to anchor soil.

title: Balanced NPK for maize
text: Maize responds to nitrogen but also needs phosphorus for root development and potassium for stalk strength. Place phosphorus near the planting hole and top-dress nitrogen at knee height. Do not apply fertiliser on dry soil without imminent rain or irrigation.

title: Organic manure application rates
text: Well-composted farmyard manure supplies slow-release nutrients and improves soil biology. Apply five to ten tonnes per hectare before planting, avoiding fresh manure on leafy vegetables. Combine manure with a modest mineral top-dress where soil tests show gaps.

title: Micronutrient boron in legumes
text: Boron deficiency causes hollow stems and poor pod set in beans on sandy acidic soils. Use foliar boron only at recommended rates because excess is toxic. Correct underlying acidity and organic matter deficits before relying on foliar sprays alone.

title: Newcastle disease in village chickens
text: Newcastle disease causes respiratory distress, greenish diarrhoea, and sudden flock mortality. Vaccinate chicks on schedule using eye-drop or drinking-water protocols from extension services. Isolate sick birds and disinfect feeders between batches.

title: Dry-season fodder conservation
text: Harvest surplus forage at boot stage and sun-dry on raised racks to make hay. Store under cover to prevent mould and nutrient loss. Supplement with mineral blocks when grazing quality falls below maintenance needs.

title: Tsetse-free corralling practices
text: Night corralling in smoke-treated pens reduces tsetse exposure for cattle in fly belts. Clear bush within fifty metres of kraals and rotate grazing away from riverine vegetation at peak fly hours. Combine community spraying with trypanosomiasis screening where veterinary services are available.

title: Hermetic storage for maize grain
text: Hermetic bags or silos exclude oxygen and stop maize weevils without chemical dust. Dry grain to twelve to thirteen percent moisture before sealing. Inspect bags monthly for punctures and reseal promptly.

title: Aflatoxin prevention in groundnuts
text: Aflatoxin risk rises when groundnuts are left damp after harvest or stored on bare soil. Dry pods quickly on raised mats and sort out mouldy kernels before bagging. Keep storage rooms ventilated and elevated off the ground.

title: Cassava chip drying standards
text: Cassava chips should be dried to below fourteen percent moisture to prevent spoilage and cyanide concerns. Slice uniformly and sun-dry on black plastic or raised racks with regular turning. Store dry chips in woven bags off the floor in a rodent-proof room.
